message.content:
Yes—you can file a noise complaint with the City of Atlanta’s local government.  
In the U.S., noise complaints are typically handled by the city’s **Police Department** or **Code Enforcement** office, and the City of Atlanta provides several convenient ways to do so.

---

## How to File a Noise Complaint in Atlanta

| Method | What to Do | Contact / Link |
|--------|------------|----------------|
| **Phone (311)** | Call the non‑emergency 311 line. The dispatcher will route your call to the appropriate department (usually Police or Code Enforcement). | 404‑656‑3111 |
| **Online Portal** | Use the City of Atlanta’s 311 online portal to submit a “Noise Complaint” form. You’ll be asked for details such as location, time, and a brief description. | <https://www.atlantaga.gov/311> |
| **Mobile App** | Download the City of Atlanta 311 app (available on iOS and Android) and file a complaint from your phone. | App Store / Google Play |
| **In‑Person** | Visit City Hall or a local police precinct. Bring any evidence (audio recordings, dates, times, photos). | City Hall: 1000 Peachtree St NW, Atlanta, GA 30303 |
| **Mail** | Send a written complaint to the City of Atlanta, Office of the City Manager, or the Police Department. | 1000 Peachtree St NW, Atlanta, GA 30303 |

---

## What the City Will Do

1. **Initial Assessment** – The dispatcher or officer will note the complaint and may ask for additional details.
2. **Investigation** – Police or Code Enforcement will investigate the alleged noise violation. They may issue a warning, citation, or order to cease the activity.
3. **Follow‑up** – If the noise continues, the city can take further action, including fines or court proceedings.

---

## Atlanta Noise Ordinance Basics

| Time | Allowed Noise Level | Typical Enforcement |
|------|---------------------|---------------------|
| Weekdays 10 p.m.–6 a.m. | Quiet hours; loud music, parties, construction, etc. are prohibited. | Police or Code Enforcement |
| Weekends 11 p.m.–6 a.m. | Quiet hours; same restrictions apply. | Police or Code Enforcement |
| Construction | Must comply with the city’s construction noise regulations (often 7 a.m.–7 p.m.). | Code Enforcement |
| Commercial | Businesses must keep noise within limits set by the city’s commercial noise ordinance. | Code Enforcement |

*Note:* The exact decibel limits and enforcement procedures are detailed in the **City of Atlanta Code, Title 12 (Public Health), Chapter 12.1 (Noise)**. You can view the full ordinance on the city’s website under “City Code” or by contacting the City Clerk’s office.

---

## Tips for a Successful Complaint

1. **Document the Noise** – Record the date, time, duration, and type of noise. Audio or video evidence can be very helpful.
2. **Check the Source** – Identify the property or business responsible. If it’s a neighbor, you might try a friendly conversation first.
3. **Be Specific** – Provide the exact address or intersection, and describe the noise (e.g., “loud music from a party at 1234 Peachtree St.”).
4. **Follow Up** – If you don’t hear back within a few days, call 311 or check the status of your online ticket.

---

## Quick Contact List

| Department | Phone | Email |
|------------|-------|-------|
| **Atlanta Police Department** | 404‑656‑3111 (non‑emergency) | [police@atlantaga.gov](mailto:police@atlantaga.gov) |
| **Code Enforcement** | 404‑656‑3111 (non‑emergency) | [code@atlantaga.gov](mailto:code@atlantaga.gov) |
| **City Clerk (City Code)** | 404‑656‑3111 | [clerk@atlantaga.gov](mailto:clerk@atlantaga.gov) |

---

### Bottom Line

Yes, you can report a noise complaint to the City of Atlanta. Use the 311 line, the online portal, or visit City Hall to file a formal complaint. The city’s Police Department or Code Enforcement will investigate and enforce the noise ordinance. If you’re dealing with a persistent problem, gathering evidence and following up will help the city take action more quickly.
